analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Oct 29..TECK beats (again), GLEN reassures, FM beats, SHEL smashes it, NESTE ditto, TTE not so much, EGO hmmm and resets....much more
key_insights: Copper: the desk says overnight price action is macro-driven with no flow through the desk. Shorts are covering and front spreads are squeezing. The desk flags growing concern about US copper tariffs imminently after the midterms, and says if tariffs are staggered and imports keep flowing to COMEX, metal will run short on other exchanges. Onshore China premiums are the watch item, and supply is the key watch into 2027.
Cochilco projects sulfuric acid consumption in copper to rise 9% (+900kt), cited by the desk as a supply-side watch item for 2027.
Iron ore: Fortescue says it will not rush a deal with CMRG, and the chair says it will not 'cave in to demands'. Fortescue's guidance partly hinges on a deal before year-end.

M&A: Northern Star rejected Gold Fields' first offer of $38.7bn ($27 per share) and is reportedly holding out for $31.50 or more. Platinum (NPH.SJ) has a 1 Dec process deadline and reports significant interest from South African and multinational parties. Boliden (BOL.SS) and Nexa are also in focus for an update.

Glencore (GLEN.LN): the desk calls the result reassuring, starting about +1%. Copper output of 202kt is inside the buyside range of 200-205kt, zinc and energy coal beat, and all FY guides are held. Copper and met coal sit at the low end of their ranges, thermal coal and zinc at the high end. The marketing guide of >$5bn was reaffirmed.

Glencore copper guide is now 810-870kt at the low end. GS models 824kt versus consensus 833kt, with Q4 estimates expected to fall 5-10kt. YTD output is 599kt, and Kazzinc is running +15% vs consensus. The desk keeps GLEN as a top pick, favouring base metals over bulks.

Boliden (BOL.SS) results were delayed to 1pm because of a board meeting. The desk expects fine numbers and an average operational update. Watch items are EBIT ex-PIR (consensus SEK 4.198bn), the Odda smelter ramp, Aitik mill throughput and the Tara restart.

Teck (TECK.CN): a very strong beat with EPS 1.88 vs 1.60 and EBITDA $2.31bn vs company consensus $2.068bn. Production guides were tightened to the high end for HVC, zinc and Trail, CDA is at the low end on weather, and QB is unchanged. Unit costs guidance was cut. The desk expects Anglo American and Teck to trade +2-3% relative on the print.

Teck Q3 production: copper 115.7kt, zinc 169kt vs consensus 159kt. QB copper was 47.2kt vs consensus 54.7kt on severe weather, HVC 35.2kt vs 29kt, and CDA 5.2kt. The desk says QB looks set for a very strong Q4 with no maintenance scheduled, and that TMF acceleration bodes well for the QB/Collahuasi JV.

Eldorado Gold (EGO.US): a full reset with production down, costs up and capex up. Q3 EBITDA was $275m vs consensus $309m and FCF was -$191m vs -$103m. Gold production was 106koz vs 112koz, AISC $2,050/oz vs $1,967/oz, and 2026 Skouries/McIlvenna Bay gold guidance was cut by 40kt (8.6% at midpoint). The desk says it remains a show-me story into year-end.

Eldorado capex: Skouries rises to $1.425bn (+$110m) and McIlvenna Bay to $975m (+$23m). Base metal guidance was cut, with copper at 10-25m lbs (previously 20-40m) and silver at 1.2-1.5m oz (previously 1.55-1.75m).

First Quantum (FM.CN): a solid beat with EPS 29c vs consensus 19c and EBITDA $844m vs $694m, starting +2-3%. Nickel at Trident, a faster Cobre Panamá ramp and the Guelb Moghrein gold transition offset the Kansanshi Cu/Au miss. The desk describes Panama restart as a 6-9 month process, with stockpiles lasting until March 2027.
First Quantum's board visited Argentina. Taca Taca is 275-300kt for $6.8bn with first production in 2035, and La Granja (Peru) is 200kt for $7.2bn.

Vale reports after the close on 29 Oct. GS expects Q3 EBITDA of $3.3bn (-20% q/q) vs consensus $3.57bn on weaker iron ore output, lower price realization and higher fuel and freight costs. GS forecasts price realization down $5/t y/y in 2027, with benchmark iron ore at $93/t for 2027 vs $100/t for 2026.
Jiangxi Copper shares fell as much as 12.7% despite a surge in Q3 profit, on concerns about further margin pressure.

Shell (SHEL): +3-4% on a 5% EBITDA beat vs consensus, a $5bn buyback and CFFO ex working capital of $21.7bn, beating consensus by $3.5bn (20%). Gearing fell to 16.6%. The desk calls it the core long in global energy.

TotalEnergies (TTE) is down 1%. Net income was +2% vs consensus, with an E&P miss and small beats in IG and marketing. CFFO ex WC was $12.3bn vs $12.1bn consensus. The desk expects it to sell off given the stock rallied into the print.

Neste is up 5%: EBITDA €1.55bn (+29% vs consensus), renewables €1.01bn vs €776m, oil products €504m vs €330m. A new 20-40% EPS payout dividend policy was announced. Rotterdam capex rose to €3bn from €2.5bn, and start-up is still expected in 2027.

Repsol (REP): +2%, adjusted net €2.9bn (5% ahead), CFFO ex WC €3.5bn, and Q3 buyback €950m. The desk would be long REP vs Galp and TTE and flags the call (QTD and spot margins) as the key risk to a fade.

OMV: down 3%. Operating profit was €2.11bn vs €2.17bn consensus, with a strong refining beat offset by very weak chemicals and a negative inventory effect. CFFO ex WC was €2.3bn vs €1.8bn, helped by lower cash taxes.
Technip Energies (TE.FP): +5%. EBITDA beat by 16%, FY guide and 2028 EBITDA target (>€800m) confirmed, margin 8.9% vs 7.1% consensus, order intake €1.4bn vs €1.13bn, and FCF conversion 87%.

China A-shares: banks hit all-time highs and insurers rose, while robotics pulled back after Unitree's R&D spending weighed on Q3 profit. CPO stocks were volatile after Alphabet's Q3 capex came in below internal estimates, reopening the debate on hyperscaler AI spending.

Other results: CIA fell 16.5% on lower prices, freight and fuel (read-across to Vale). LYC production was 16% above consensus and flagged a full Malaysia maintenance shutdown in December, which the desk links to global rare earth supply.

market_movers.rationale: Glencore remains a top pick as GS favours base metals over bulks. Results cleared the bar, guides were held, and the stock is at 540p.
The desk calls Shell the core long in global energy after a 5% EBITDA beat, a $5bn buyback and CFFO ex WC of $21.7bn.
Teck's very strong beat and tightened high-end guides lead the desk to expect Anglo American and Teck to trade +2-3% relative on the print.
Repsol was good enough on the quarter, and the desk would be long vs Galp and TTE, but warns it could fade on macro with the call focused on QTD and spot margins.
TotalEnergies rallied into the print, numbers were in line, and the desk thinks it will sell off given Shell's stronger result.
Eldorado reset production, costs and capex lower. The desk says the market was conditioned for it and it stays a show-me story into year-end.

sector_views.rationale: GS favours base metals over bulks, citing Glencore as a top pick, tight copper supply into 2027 and Teck's strong operating delivery.
Shell is described as the core long in global energy after a strong beat. Repsol is preferred over Galp and TotalEnergies.
GS downgraded Vale on weaker production, fuel and freight costs, and lower price realization, with benchmark iron ore forecast at $93/t for 2027 vs $100/t for 2026.

earnings_insights: Teck Q3 (reported 29 Oct): EPS $1.88 reported vs $1.60 prior-period comparator as the report states it, EBITDA $2.31bn vs company-compiled consensus $2.068bn. Production guides tightened to the high end and unit costs guidance cut.
First Quantum Q3 (reported): EPS $0.29 vs consensus $0.19, EBITDA $844m vs consensus $694m. Guidance a little lower, as expected.

Eldorado Gold Q3 (reported): EBITDA $275m vs consensus $309m, FCF -$191m vs consensus -$103m, gold production 106koz vs consensus 112koz, cash cost $1,415/oz vs $1,451/oz consensus, AISC $2,050/oz vs $1,967/oz consensus.

Glencore Q3 production update (reported 29 Oct): copper 202kt inside the buyside range of 200-205kt, zinc and energy coal beat consensus. Kazzinc is +15% vs consensus. FY copper guide is 810-870kt, GS estimates 824kt vs consensus 833kt.
Boliden (reporting 29 Oct at 1pm): consensus EBIT ex-PIR is SEK 4.198bn.
Vale (reporting after the close 29 Oct): GS estimates Q3 EBITDA of $3.3bn (-20% q/q) vs consensus $3.57bn.
Shell Q3 (reported): EBITDA about 5% above consensus, net income about 5% above consensus, CFFO ex working capital $21.7bn (about $3.5bn or 20% above consensus), $5bn buyback, gearing 16.6%.
TotalEnergies Q3 (reported): net income +2% vs consensus, CFFO ex WC $12.3bn vs $12.1bn consensus.
Neste Q3 (reported): EBITDA €1.55bn (+29% vs consensus), renewables €1.01bn vs €776m consensus, oil products €504m vs €330m consensus.
Repsol Q3 (reported): adjusted net income €2.9bn (5% above consensus), CFFO ex WC €3.5bn (+4% vs consensus), Q3 buyback €950m.
OMV Q3 (reported): operating profit €2.11bn vs €2.17bn consensus, CFFO ex WC €2.3bn vs €1.8bn consensus.
Technip Energies Q3 (reported): EBITDA 16% above consensus, margin 8.9% vs 7.1% consensus, order intake €1.4bn vs €1.13bn consensus, FCF conversion 87% excluding working capital and provisions.
CIA (pre-reported) fell 16.5%. LYC production was 16% above consensus.

tension_points.bull_case: Copper output of 202kt sits inside the buyside range, and YTD output of 599kt plus a 4Q25 comparison of 268kt leaves a buffer against the 810-870kt guide.
tension_points.bear_case: Some investors are negative on the copper guide now sitting at the low end of its range, and Africa's big step-up is not repeatable.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q4 production falling short of the buffer needed to reach the low end of 810-870kt.

tension_points.bull_case: Staggered tariffs in steel and aluminium came with downstream investment announcements, a precedent for a manageable outcome.
tension_points.bear_case: If tariffs arrive and imports continue to COMEX, other exchanges will run out of metal, and the market is already squeezed at the front.
